text: Meeting deadlines can feel overwhelming, but a few practical habits make it manageable. First, practice time management by breaking large projects into smaller tasks and setting mini-deadlines for each one. This prevents last-minute panic. Next, learn prioritization—identify which tasks are most important or urgent, and tackle those first. Additionally, be honest about scope management: if a request is unrealistic, don't silently struggle. Instead, communicate early with your manager or client. Explain what’s possible within the given time and suggest adjusting the requirements. Regular updates also build trust. Ultimately, deadlines aren’t just about speed; they’re about planning, talking openly, and delivering quality work without sacrificing your well-being.
